column2: How do I find out whether an heir has since died (INSEE death file)?
column3: File → 👥 Heirs → “⚰️ Check deaths”: the “living” heirs are compared with the INSEE file already imported, under their birth name (never a married name), with a score out of 100. Nothing changes without your click: “✓ This is the person” records the death (setting), “✕ Not the same person” is remembered. “Nothing found” does not mean “alive”.

column2: How do I send a questionnaire to an heir?
column3: ✉️ Heirs contacted → “📋 Questionnaire…”: tick the heirs and what you are asking. The .html file opens with a double-click, without internet; the heir sends you back their answers. “⤒ Import answers…” shows them field by field: nothing is written without your review, and a modified file is refused.

column2: Where do I note my calls and exchanges with the heirs?
column3: In the file, “📞 Contacts” tab (or in 👥 Heirs, depending on the setting): when, with whom, how, the summary and the next step. With a date, a deadline goes into the 🔔 bell (never the summary).

column2: How do I track a registered letter and its acknowledgement of receipt?
column3: On a letter: “📮” → the number, the sending date and the date of the receipt. With no receipt after 15 days (adjustable), the 🔔 bell reminds you. The app does not query La Poste: the link opens the tracking page in your browser.

column2: How do I make a quote or an invoice?
column3: 💶 Time and costs → “🧾 Make an invoice”: the lines are suggested (commission, costs, time). You type the VAT rate and the legal notes yourself (🏢 My office, with your accountant). Numbers follow each other with no gap; an issued invoice can no longer be changed: a credit note corrects it.

column2: Where can I see my office’s activity?
column3: ⚖️ Estates → “📈 Activity”: open files, average time until handover, contracts signed or refused, invoiced and collected, time per file. No heir names; nothing is written.

column2: How do I send a copy of the file to the notary?
column3: 🖨 For the notary → “🤝 Copy to send to the notary…”: an .html file the notary opens with a double-click, without being able to change it, encrypted with a password if you wish (give it by another channel). The log, contacts and invoices never leave.

column2: How do I see on a map where the heirs live?
column3: 👥 Heirs → “🗺 See on the map” (or ⚖️ Estates → ⋯ for all open files): one dot per municipality, from the Register of the living, and the notaries the app knows. Nothing is sent online.

column2: How do I use my own revelation contract?
column3: ✉️ Heirs contacted → “📝 My contract templates”: write or import your text (.docx or .txt), with fields like {nom}, {pourcentage}, {siret}. Each version is kept and each filed contract remembers its own. The app provides no contract text.

column2: How do I track money received from the notary and paid out to the heirs?
column3: 💶 Time and costs → “💶 Funds per heir”: note what the notary’s office paid you, the commission, the costs and what you paid out; the app works out what is still due. No estate amount is kept, only your real movements.

column2: What is the “double proof” of a link?
column3: 📑 Documents → 🔗 banner: for each parentage link, the number of documents that prove it (two copies of the same record count as one). A link with a single document is “to review” before handover; “✓ One document is enough here” notes it in the log.

column2: How do I get reminded of a date given by the notary?
column3: 📁 File → “＋ An important date”: the date, what has to be done and where it comes from (required). The 🔔 bell warns you at D−30, D−7 and D−1 (adjustable). The app computes no legal deadline.

column2: How do I bring two files together (a couple who died a few months apart)?
column3: In the file, ⋯ → “👥 Merge with another file…”: the preview says what happens. Two deceased, two calculations side by side (or files only linked, setting). ↶ Undo separates them again for 30 days.

column2: Where can I see the searches made for an heir?
column3: 👥 Heirs → 🕵️ on the row: the notes from the Research log, the INSEE checks and the contacts marked “search”. “Nothing found” counts too; they can be attached to the notary’s copy.

column2: How do I archive a closed file with a password?
column3: Closed file → ⋯ → “🗄 Archive to a file and remove…”: the file also takes the contacts, the funds and a copy of the invoices, encrypted with a password (setting: offered, required or not offered). Forgotten = archive lost; re-importing asks for it.

column2: An heir died after the deceased: how do I open their estate?
column3: 👥 Heirs → “🔗 Open a linked file” on their row: a new file for them, with their descendants attached (setting); the two files point to each other.

column2: How do I ask the same office for several records in a single letter?
column3: 📑 Documents → “📮 One letter per office”: the missing records are grouped by town hall; reread each letter, then file them in the Letter register. The documents switch to “Requested”.

column2: How long does a town hall take to answer?
column3: ⚖️ Estates → ⋯ → “⏳ Response time by office”: from sending to the answer received, based on your record requests (average or median, setting).

column2: How do I get warned that a copy of a record is getting too old?
column3: 📑 Documents → 📅 on the row: the issue date and the validity period your notary asks for (none by default). The 🔔 bell warns you beforehand.

column2: How do I hide names and amounts during a video call?
column3: In the file, ⋯ → “🙈 Shared screen”: names become initials (or numbers), addresses and amounts are hidden, without leaving the file. A second click restores everything.

column2: Where do I change the settings of these file tools?
column3: Settings → Appearance → 🧭 How you use the app → “⚖️ File tools: settings” (or “⚙️ Settings for this tool” in each window). Each choice has a help sentence; the recommended option is the starting one.
